_source: CONFIRMED ON REAL HARDWARE: a Pulsar X2H mini with its 4K wireless
dongle. Battery, firmware version, polling rate (up to 4000 Hz,
confirming the dongle really is the 4K variant), motion sync, angle
snap, ripple control, turbo mode, lift-off distance, debounce, sleep
timer, and DPI stage 1's value and LED colour have all round-tripped
real writes on that exact hardware, not just plausible-looking reads --
the LED colour write the owner visually confirmed actually changed the
mouse's light. Cable and the 2.4GHz dongle both present the identical
3554:f507 identity on the identical hidraw node -- there is no separate
wired/wireless split for this model.
ONLY DPI STAGE 1 IS MAPPED, DELIBERATELY. This plugin's own design
choice, not a hardware limitation of the other stages' storage --
dpiStage2/3/4 and their colours DO read and write correctly (confirmed
before this decision), but nothing was ever found that makes the mouse
actually USE a stage other than whichever is 'active': activeDpiStage
writes round-trip correctly (the byte stores and reads back) but never
changed the mouse's live output, and the mouse's own physical DPI
button doesn't switch stages either. Rather than ship a 4-stage
selector where only one stage visibly does anything, this profile only
reads/writes stage 1, and the panel shows a single DPI slider + colour
field instead of a stage list. The other stages' addresses are still
documented in the _dpiComment below for whoever eventually finds the
real switch mechanism (see _followUp).
IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this has only been verified against the 4K dongle
variant. Pulsar sells the X2H mini with either a 1K or a 4K dongle;
if you have the 1K variant, the polling-rate ceiling and possibly the
USB ids could differ -- please report back what you find, and expect
`uiOptions`/`values` on `pollingRate` to need adjusting for that variant.
Recovered in three stages, cheapest first:
1. Community Linux tools already speaking Pulsar's Nordic protocol --
packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux (drivers/nordic.py, an
address-mapped memory protocol for VID 0x3554) and
andrewrabert/python-pulsar-mouse-tool, its credited source -- gave
the packet shape (17 bytes, opcode + address + length,
sum8_minus_55 checksum) and the command/address table, but not this
exact model's USB ids, nor (initially) the right report id/transport.
2. Static analysis of the real Pulsar Fusion Windows installer
(tools/analyze-driver.py, recovered from git history, pointed at
the innoextract'd 'Pulsar Fusion Wireless Mice.exe' and the Cfg.ini
it ships) confirmed real USB ids (Cfg.ini's [OPT]:
VID=25A7,3554 PID=fa7b,f507 PID2=fa7c,f508,f509) and this exact
model's defaults (Cfg.ini's [DEV_13]: Sensor=0x3395/PAW3395,
DPI=400,800,1600,3200, Debounce=3) -- capability metadata, not wire
protocol, since the app is native C++/MFC and embeds its actual
packet-building logic as machine code, not an extractable blob the
way a .NET app's byte-array literals were for the G-Wolves profile.
3. hskctl probe/status/set against the real device caught what steps 1
and 2 could not: the actual transport is a raw USB Output report at
report id 8 (not the Feature-report id 6 the HID descriptor's own
feature-report field first suggested), and every scalar write
needs a second checksum byte (0x55 - value) immediately after the
value -- both now implemented in protocol.py as transport.kind:
"output" (already existed) and the valueChecksum command option
(added for this). DPI stages needed a new `nordicDpi3` field
encoding, cross-checked byte-for-byte against the real driver's own
_dpi_to_raw/_raw_to_dpi for several DPI values before ever touching
hardware with it.

match._comment: vendorIds/productIds match Cfg.ini's own [OPT] block from the real Pulsar Fusion installer (VID=25A7,3554  PID=fa7b,f507  PID2=fa7c,f508,f509) and what `hskctl probe` finds live on real hardware: the mouse enumerates as 3554:f507 (config endpoint on interface 11, vendor usage page 0xff04, feature report id 6) -- and, confirmed by the owner, that is the SAME identity and same hidraw node whether the mouse is connected by cable or through its 2.4GHz dongle. There is no separate 'wired' vs 'wireless' profile split for this model: the dongle appears to tunnel the mouse's own USB identity through transparently rather than exposing a distinct config interface of its own. The receiver's other USB identity, 3554:f509 ('Pulsar 4K Wireless Receiver'), is kept in match.productIds in case some other pairing state exposes it differently, but every read and write confirmed so far went through 3554:f507 regardless of physical connection. 25a7:fa7b/fa7c are Cfg.ini's alternate ids (presumably an older USB bridge chip revision) with no hardware here to confirm them against. Do NOT add 0x3710:0x1403 (X2H Wired Medium) to this profile: that model speaks a different, 64-byte, register-addressed protocol (the one x2a.py/x2h.py implement), not the 17-byte memory-mapped one this file describes -- it needs its own profile.

transport._comment: Corrected against the real, cloned source of packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux (not a secondhand summary): drivers/nordic.py and drivers/x2_crazylight.py -- the latter decoded from an actual Pulsar Fusion USB capture (GitHub issue #7), independent of the former -- both agree the transport is a raw USB Output report (SET_REPORT, wValue high byte 0x02) with report id 0x08, read back over the interrupt IN endpoint, NOT a Feature report (HIDIOCGFEATURE/HIDIOCSFEATURE) as first guessed from `hskctl probe`'s feature report id 6 on this interface. hskctl's existing transport.kind: "output" already implements exactly this shape (write_output = os.write, read_input = os.read) with no engine changes needed -- byte 0 of every command template below is now 0x08 to match.

commands._comment: Two shapes here. 'battery'/'version' are their own opcodes (byte 1) with data from byte 2, matching the G-Wolves style. Everything else rides the dongle's memory-mapped get/set (opcode 0x08 read / 0x07 write, at a fixed address baked into each command's template since every hskctl field is its own fixed address, not a runtime parameter) -- byte 3:4 address (endianness unconfirmed, written big-endian here), byte 5 length, value from byte 6.

battery._note: [6]=percent, [7]=power/charging, [8:10]=millivolts per the nordic.py summary. Only percent and charging are mapped here; battery_mv would need a u16 field of its own once confirmed.

pollingRate._note: address 0x00. Raw<->Hz table confirmed from packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux's real source (drivers/nordic.py POLL_HZ_TO_VAL) -- 125/2000/4000/8000 credited there to an actual Pulsar Fusion USB capture (github.com/packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux issue #7 on the X2 CrazyLight, a different model sharing this same Nordic register map), 250/500/1000 to andrewrabert's earlier tool. The encoding itself (which raw byte means which rate) is solid; which of these seven rates the X2H mini specifically offers in Fusion's UI is not confirmed -- see the field's uiOptions note.

sleep._note: address 0xb7, described as 'units of 10s'; encoded below with scale:10 so the field itself still speaks seconds.

commands._dpiComment: DPI stages are 4-byte records (ADDR_DPI_BASE=0x0C, DPI_STAGE_SIZE=4 per drivers/nordic.py): 3 data bytes (nordicDpi3 encoding) + 1 valueChecksum byte, same mechanism as every scalar field above just with a 3-byte value instead of 1. LED colour is the same shape at ADDR_LED_COLOR_BASE=0x2C (rgb encoding, still 3 bytes + checksum). Byte 5 (length) is 3 for reads (only the 3 data bytes are decoded) and 4 for writes (3 value bytes + the checksum byte the device actually stores). Only stage 1's address is mapped here -- this plugin deliberately only ever reads/writes DPI stage 1, see the note on the `dpiStage1` field below for why.

batteryPercent._note: Confirmed on real hardware: reads a plausible, stable percentage across repeated status calls.

charging._note: Confirmed on real hardware: correctly flips true/false matching the cable actually being plugged in or not.

firmwareVersion._note: Confirmed on real hardware: reads a plausible, stable major.minor version (2.24) across repeated status calls.

pollingRate._note: 1000 <-> 4000 Hz round-tripped exactly on real hardware (`hskctl set pollingRate 4000` read back 4000, then 1000 read back 1000), confirming both the raw<->Hz table and the write path for this field specifically, not just by analogy to motionSync. 8000 is left out of uiOptions -- the owner's dongle is specifically a '4K' model, so 8000 is unconfirmed and plausibly unreachable; the `values` map still has it in case a future capture confirms it.

dpiStageCount._note: Briefly unlocked to test whether dpiStageCount=1 explained activeDpiStage writes having no live effect (a reasonable theory: the real driver's own logic gates how many stages the firmware considers live on this count). Setting it to 4 -- Cfg.ini's real factory default, not a guess -- had a real, confirmed side effect (it reset the DPI table to factory defaults, overwriting a custom stage 1 value/colour that had been set moments earlier) but did NOT fix stage switching: activeDpiStage still had no live effect afterward, and the physical DPI button does nothing either. Reverted to 1 (the owner's actual working setup) and locked read-only again -- not because writing it is inherently unsafe, but because it has a real destructive side effect and no longer serves a purpose now that this plugin only ever uses stage 1.

activeDpiStage._note: Kept mapped for diagnostics only -- not used by this plugin's UI, and not confirmed to do anything: the write round-trips (byte stores and reads back correctly) but has no observed live effect on the mouse, and the physical DPI button doesn't switch stages either. Wire value is 0-based; `add: 1` still applies for anyone reading/writing it directly via hskctl, matching the 1-based convention used elsewhere. If a future real capture finds the actual stage-switch mechanism, this is the field to revisit.

liftOffDistance._note: Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary. Read value (1mm) is a plausible default, not independently cross-checked.

debounceMs._note: Read value (3) is an EXACT match to the real Pulsar Fusion installer's Cfg.ini [DEV_13] factory default (Debounce=3) for this model. Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary.

motionSync._note: CANARY FIELD: unverified marker deliberately removed first, alone, to test the new valueChecksum write path on real hardware before trusting it for every other field. Confirm `hskctl set motionSync off` then `hskctl get motionSync` (and the reverse) round-trip correctly before removing _needsVerification from anything else in this profile.

angleSnap._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same mechanism, different address).

rippleControl._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same mechanism, different address).

turboMode._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same mechanism, different address).

sleepSeconds._note: Read value (30s) confirmed correct by the owner against their actual mouse's real auto-sleep behavior. Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary.

dpiStage1._note: Confirmed on real hardware: `hskctl set dpiStage1 3200` round-tripped exactly and the mouse's actual cursor speed changed. Only stage 1 is mapped, deliberately -- live switching to stages 2-4 turned out not to work on this firmware via any mechanism found (activeDpiStage writes round-trip but have no live effect, and the physical DPI button does nothing either), so this plugin only ever reads/writes stage 1 rather than exposing a switcher that looks like it works but does not.

dpiStage1Color._note: Confirmed on real hardware: the LED visibly changed to the set colour. Only stage 1's colour is mapped, same reasoning as dpiStage1.

_followUp: KNOWN LIMITATION, not a bug to chase further without a real capture: switching which DPI stage is live doesn't work by any mechanism found. activeDpiStage writes round-trip (byte stores and reads back correctly) but never change the mouse's actual output, and the physical DPI button does nothing either. dpiStageCount was briefly tried as the explanation (the real driver's own logic gates on it) -- setting it to 4 reset the whole DPI table to factory defaults but did not fix switching, so it was reverted to 1 and locked read-only again. The real mechanism is most likely a dedicated command distinct from the plain memory writes nordic.py assumes for a different model (compare CMD_ACTIVE_PROFILE_SET, a separate opcode for switching *profiles*, not stages) -- finding it needs a live USB capture (Wireshark/usbmon) of Pulsar Fusion actually switching stages, per docs/PROTOCOL-DISCOVERY.md's method.

Given that, this plugin deliberately only reads/writes DPI stage 1 (see the note on the model's own _source block above) rather than exposing a 4-stage selector where only one stage visibly works. dpiStage2/3/4 and their colours were confirmed to read/write correctly before this decision -- their addresses are ADDR_DPI_BASE + 4*n and ADDR_LED_COLOR_BASE + 4*n (see _dpiComment) if a future capture finds the real switch mechanism and this profile should re-expose them.

1K dongle variant unconfirmed -- if you have one, check whether it matches this profile's USB ids at all (`hskctl probe`), and whether pollingRate above 1000 Hz actually works (`hskctl set pollingRate 2000`) or the firmware rejects/clamps it. Adjust `values`/`uiOptions` accordingly; it may need a separate profile if the ids differ.

The RF receiver's separate USB identity (3554:f509) has never actually been seen carrying the config protocol -- every confirmed read/write went through 3554:f507, dongle or cable alike. Plausibly unused for config and droppable from match.productIds, but no positive evidence either way, so it stays for now.

pollingRate's `values` map includes 8000 Hz (from the real source, confirmed on a different Nordic-family model) but `uiOptions` stops at 4000 since this is specifically the 4K dongle -- do not widen it without an 8K dongle to test against.

Two low-risk gaps vs. the real driver, neither able to corrupt a setting: autosleep is written to 0xB7 only here, but the real driver mirrors the same value to 0xAD too (ADDR_AUTOSLEEP_ALT) -- needs a 'write to two addresses' hook if the firmware actually requires both in sync. And unsolicited reports (e.g. opcode 0x0A after a profile switch) can desync a naive read-once -- the real driver retries until resp[1] matches the opcode sent; check_ack here only supports a fixed expected byte, not 'echo the sent opcode'.
